arXiv:2511.21983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a quantum sensing protocol for coupled qubit-oscillator systems that surpasses the standard quantum limit (SQL) by exploiting a geometrical phase. The signal is encoded in the geometrical phase that is proportional to the area enclosed in oscillator phase space. This area is amplified through squeezing, enabling sensitivities beyond the SQL. Our method is independent of oscillator's initial state, amenable to sensing with high-temperature or logical error-corrected states. The protocol shows robustness to qubit Markovian noise and preserves its state-independence, underscoring its practicality for next-generation quantum metrology. arXiv:2512.05496v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretically secure communication against eavesdropping. arXiv:2610.35119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In classical simulations of quantum circuits, sampling shots (measurement outcomes) from the final state is a routine but costly step. In widely used software, including Qiskit and PennyLane, its cost grows linearly with the number of shots S, even when the simulation has already produced the full state vector, because every shot is generated and processed individually. If only the measurement counts are needed, this is unnecessary. The counts can be drawn directly from a multinomial distribution, decomposed into a sequence of conditional binomial draws, each performed in expected constant time by the BTPE algorithm. item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yu-Hao Chen, Renata Wong
arXiv:2601.07890v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work provides a step-by-step quantum computing derivation of the unitary coupled cluster singles and doubles ansatz. We show how the structure of the ansatz emerges from fermionic algebra under unitary constraints. By explicitly connecting second quantization, Jordan-Wigner mapping, and quantum circuit synthesis, we clarify conceptual gaps between quantum physics and quantum computing implementations, particularly regarding operator locality, commutation structure, and hardware realization. We exemplify the procedure on the singles and doubles coupled cluster ansatz for the hydrogen molecule.

The resulting variational circuits can be tailored to the connectivity and long-range interaction of the target hardware.
